items.text: COMMITTEE DISCHARGED AND COMMITTED TO EDUCATION

items.actClause: AN ACT to amend the education law, in relation to background checks and fingerprinting; and to amend the social services law, in relation to statewide central registry clearances by contracted service providers of student support services
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER:  S3479

 TITLE OF BILL :  An act to amend the education law, in relation to
background checks and fingerprinting; and to amend the social services
law, in relation to statewide central registry clearances by
contracted service providers of student support services

 PURPOSE :

To require the fingerprinting of prospective nonpublic and private
elementary and secondary school employees, and make such information
available to contracted service providers of student support services.

 SUMMARY OF SPECIFIC PROVISIONS :

Section one amends subdivision 3 of section 1125 of the education law

Section two amends subdivision 3 of section 2854 of the education law

Section three will amend subdivision 30 of section 305 of the
education law

Section four amends opening paragraph of subdivision 30 of section 305
of the education law

Section five amends subdivision 30 of section 305 of the education law

Section six amends subdivision 31 of section 305 of the education law

Section seven will amend subdivision 1 of section 3035 of the
education law

Section eight amends subdivision 3 of section 3035 of the education
law

Section nine amends subdivision 3 of section 3035 of the education law

Section ten amends section 1125 of the education law by adding new
subdivision 10

Section eleven amends subdivision 3 of section 424-a of the social
services law

Section twelve amends subdivision 2 of section 390-a of the social
services law

Section thirteen sets forth the effective date

 JUSTIFICATION :

Currently, New York State school districts, BOCES, charter and
independent schools must manage the fingerprint process of all
prospective employees, including substitute teachers who may only work
temporarily. This process has proved to be quite burdensome for school
administrators as third-party providers are unable to assist in the
process.

Additionally, employers must perform the fingerprinting process for
each employee even if that employee will only work one or two days at
a particular school. Upon processing each prospective employee's
fingerprints, their Social Security numbers and other personal
information must be logged into the system. The current regulations
allow for this information to be accessed by numerous school
personnel, creating potential for serious privacy issues for school
employees. Any subsequent notifications of arrest of current or

previous employees may be missed due to the high volume of staff
records that must be maintained solely by school administrators.

This bill allow schools to contract with third-party providers of
student support services to submit and review fingerprinting and
background check data, receive results of such checks, and receive any
subsequent arrest notifications of employees. These services will be
conducted through a web-based portal developed by the State Education
Department. This act will alleviate a heavy burden on school
administrators and the State Education Department while increasing the
safety of employees and students.

 PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY :

2016: S. 7554 Rules

 FISCAL IMPLICATIONS :

Undetermined.

 EFFECTIVE DATE :
This act shall take effect immediately; provided however that: (a) the
amendments to paragraph (a-2) of subdivision 3 of section 2854 of the
education law made by section two of this act shall not affect the
expiration of such paragraph and shall expire and be deemed repealed
therewith; (b) the amendments to paragraph (d) of subdivision 30 of
section 305 of the education law made by section five of this act
shall not affect the repeal of such paragraph and shall be deemed
repealed therewith; and (c) the amendments to subdivision 3 of section
3035 of the education law made by section eight of this act shall be
subject to the expiration and reversion of such subdivision, pursuant
to section 12 of chapter 142 of the laws of 2001, as amended, when
upon such date the provisions of section nine of this act shall take
effect.
